evidence_scope: uncommitted M3 working tree based on source_commit

toolchain.process_model: three independent test processes, each holding its own locked and formatted data directory

commands.result: all M0 through M3 packages passed
all storage regressions, Raft acceptance tests, deterministic models, and subprocess tests passed
all M0 through M3 packages and the three-process driver passed under the race detector

acceptance.RP-01: same-term duplicate vote for one candidate is idempotent, a competing candidate is rejected, and model checks allow at most one leader per term
acceptance.RP-02: injected hardstate sync failure emits no vote response; a synced vote survives node reconstruction and fences a competing same-term candidate
acceptance.RP-03: RequestVote freshness uses lexicographic last term/index, rejecting a larger-index candidate whose last term is older
acceptance.RP-04: prev-term conflict hints drive uncommitted suffix repair; duplicate entries are idempotent and same index/term with different bytes is corruption
acceptance.RP-05: a majority-held old-term entry does not advance commit until the new leader's current-term NOOP reaches durable quorum and is applied
acceptance.RP-06: after isolating the old leader, the other two voters elect a higher-term ready leader; the old leader cannot commit a local proposal or complete ReadIndex
acceptance.RP-07: three real processes retain committed DATA across leader SIGKILL, majority failover, continued writes, all-process SIGKILL/restart, replay, and a new NOOP barrier; a single RF3 voter cannot elect itself

per_event_assertions: at most one observed leader per term
all pairs of nodes have byte-identical overlapping committed prefixes

additional_results: RF1 commits and applies its leader NOOP and later proposal using a one-voter quorum.
Follower leader_commit is capped at the prefix verified by that AppendEntries RPC, so an unverified local extra tail is not committed by a heartbeat.
ReadIndex completes on a healthy leader only after a current-term majority response and remains pending on an isolated old leader.
Election timeout selection uses an injected random source for the specified 600-1200 ms range at 100 ms ticks.
Every M0-M2 format, storage, crash recovery, sparse-index, and truncation regression remains in the full gate.
output_location: This scrubbed evidence manifest; no payload bytes, credentials, or large process artifacts are retained.
limitations: The M3 Node serializes durable-log calls inside Step/Tick/proposal handling; it does not yet pipeline parallel disk operations.
The subprocess driver is a test harness, not a long-running cmd/mkfk broker or public API server.
M3 has no ISR observation, HW exposure, captured acknowledgement set, min_isr admission, or public acks=all success response; these belong to M4.
Producer identity, retry deduplication, consumer groups, retention, snapshots, and Kafka wire compatibility do not exist.
next_task: M4: implement per-term follower catch-up/ISR observation, committed DATA HW mapping, captured-A acknowledgement gates, unknown-outcome timeouts, and bounded committed-prefix fetch; verify RP-08 through RP-11 and relevant OP-03/OP-04 cases.
